sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会推出的一档双周播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·露娜。

sentences.en: Just a reminder before we get started, we love to hear from our listeners.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前提醒一下，我们非常喜欢听取听众的反馈。

sentences.en: You can email your comments and ideas to kluna at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以将你的评论和想法发送至 kluna @

sentences.en: That's K-L-U-N-A at A-P-A dot org.
sentences.zh: 也就是 K-L-U-N-A 拼音加上 A-P-A 点 org。

sentences.en: Also, please consider rating us in iTunes.
sentences.zh: 此外，也请考虑在 iTunes 上为我们评分。

sentences.en: We'd really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的非常感激。

sentences.en: Some of us recall high school as being filled with fun parties, football games, and flirting, while others think back to that time with a shudder and are just glad it's over.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人回忆起高中时，充斥着有趣的派对、橄榄球比赛和调情，而另一些人则不寒而栗地回想起那段时光，只庆幸它终于结束了。

sentences.en: But is it really over?
sentences.zh: 但它真的结束了吗？

sentences.en: Does our social status as teens follow us for the rest of our lives?
sentences.zh: 我们十几岁时的社会地位会伴随我们一生吗？

sentences.en: And can we raise today's children and teens differently in our ever-status-obsessed culture?
sentences.zh: 在我们这个日益痴迷于地位的文化中，我们能否以不同的方式抚养当今的儿童和青少年？

sentences.en: Our guest for this episode is Dr. Mitch Prinstein, a clinical child and adolescent psychologist who is a John Van Cedars Distinguished Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience
sentences.zh: 本期节目的嘉宾是米奇·普林斯坦博士，他是一位临床儿童与青少年心理学家，担任心理学与神经科学的约翰·范·西达尔杰出教授

sentences.en: and the Director of Clinical Psychology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
sentences.zh: 同时也是北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的临床心理学主任。

sentences.en: Dr. Prinstein wrote the book, Popular, Finding Happiness and Success in a World That Cares
sentences.zh: 普林斯坦博士写了一本书：《受欢迎：在一个过度关心错误关系的世界里寻找幸福与成功》

sentences.en: Too Much About the Wrong Kinds of Relationships.
sentences.zh: 过度关心了错误的关系。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Prinstein.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，普林斯坦博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I'm sure many adults listening to this podcast are probably being teleported back to their teenage years and are thinking about the cool kids in school, the not-so-popular kids,
sentences.zh: 我确信很多收听这个播客的成年人可能会被带回到他们的青少年时期，并会想起学校里那些酷炫的孩子、不太受欢迎的孩子，

sentences.en: and where they themselves fit into that social hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 以及他们自己在那个社会阶层中处于什么位置。

sentences.en: Why does thinking about popularity instantly take us back to those days of middle school and high school?
sentences.zh: 为什么一想到受欢迎，就会瞬间把我们带回到初中和那段高中日子？

sentences.en: Yeah, it might be a nightmare for some people because we do go right back there, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，对某些人来说这可能是一场噩梦，因为我们的确一下子又回去了，对吧？

sentences.en: We kind of remember what it was like walking down the halls and who we might have had a crush on and who we wanted to be as popular as.
sentences.zh: 我们有点记起走在走廊里的感觉，我们可能暗恋过谁，以及我们想成为像谁一样受欢迎的人。

sentences.en: And some people kind of try and forget it all.
sentences.zh: 有些人则试图把这一切都忘掉。

sentences.en: But there's really interesting psych research now that tells us that every day as we experience
sentences.zh: 但现在有一些非常有趣的心理学研究告诉我们，每天当我们经历

sentences.en: anything, any interaction that we have, any kind of social opportunity, it somehow is all filtered through our memories.
sentences.zh: 任何事情、任何互动、任何形式的社交机会时，它们不知何故都通过我们的记忆进行了过滤。

sentences.en: And the time when these adult brains were built is the transition to adolescence.
sentences.zh: 而这些成年人大脑建构的时期，正是向青少年过渡的时期。

sentences.en: What was the most important thing to us back then?
sentences.zh: 那时候对我们来说最重要的是什么？

sentences.en: It was popularity.
sentences.zh: 那就是受欢迎。

sentences.en: So we are kind of viewing the world today through a filter or a lens that has a lot to do with our high school popularity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天看待世界的方式，其实是通过一个与我们在高中的受欢迎程度息息相关的滤镜或镜头。

sentences.en: Going off of what you just said, many of us remember wanting to be accepted in middle school but maybe not understanding exactly why that was the case.
sentences.zh: 接着你刚才的话说，我们很多人都记得在初中时渴望被接纳，但可能并不完全理解为什么会这样。

sentences.en: And in your book, you explain that it's because of brain changes that happen during puberty that make us all of a sudden worried about status.
sentences.zh: 你在书中解释说，这是因为青春期发生的大脑变化，让我们突然开始担心地位。

sentences.en: Why does that happen?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: So we don't know exactly why, but there's good evolutionary theory that tells us that it used to be that when you turn 12 or 13, you need to start getting prepared to fend for
sentences.zh: 所以我们并不确切知道原因，但有很好的进化理论告诉我们，过去当你长到12或13岁时，你需要开始准备照顾

sentences.en: yourself and learn autonomy.
sentences.zh: 自己并学会独立。

sentences.en: So the brain very cleverly kind of produces a bunch of neurotransmitters and receptors for oxytocin and for dopamine.
sentences.zh: 所以大脑非常巧妙地产生了一堆神经递质，以及催产素和多巴胺的受体。

sentences.en: So in other words, as we transition into adolescence, we become really excited about social bonding with peers and it feels really, really good when we do.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当我们过渡到青少年期时，我们对与同龄人的社交建立变得非常兴奋，而且当我们这样做时，感觉真的非常好。

sentences.en: And that kind of combination inspired us to go out and be independent and start to think that our parents have become totally lame.
sentences.zh: 这种组合激发我们走出去并变得独立，开始觉得我们的父母变得完全落伍了。

sentences.en: Today, we kind of see the same thing.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们也能看到类似的情况。

sentences.en: So just before you see changes in someone's body for puberty, you'll notice that they are really, really invested in how their social relationships are working.
sentences.zh: 因此，就在你看到某人的身体出现青春期变化之前，你会注意到他们非常、非常关注他们的社交关系是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So it's at this age where those social relationships, friendships become much more important than the relationship between a parent and child, right?
sentences.zh: 所以正是在这个年龄，这些社交关系、友谊变得比父母和孩子之间的关系重要得多，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And why does social status as teens matter when we're adults?
sentences.zh: 为什么青少年时期的社会地位在我们成年后依然重要？

sentences.en: I mean, many people would think that, you know, that was a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多人会认为，你知道，那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Who I was at 13, 14, 15, 16 is not who I am today.
sentences.zh: 我在13、14、15、16岁时的我，并不是今天的我。

sentences.en: Why does it matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么它还重要？

sentences.en: Well, it's not who we are, but yet there's a little piece of us that might still be there that still is influencing us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，虽然这不是现在的我们，但我们内心深处仍然有一小部分可能还在那里，并且仍在影响着我们。

sentences.en: It's what psychologists call social information processing, which is really just a fancy way of saying that what it is that we notice when we're looking out in the environment, we
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学家所说的社会信息处理，这其实是一个高级的说法，意思是当我们环顾周围环境时我们所注意到的是什么，我们

sentences.en: have hundreds and thousands of things we could be paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 有成百上千的事情可以去关注。

sentences.en: And how we interpret those things that we select to attend to, all of that is based on how we felt back in adolescence.
sentences.zh: 而我们如何解释那些我们选择去关注的事物，所有这一切都基于我们在青春期时的感受。

sentences.en: So if you are somebody who is rejected, you might see rejection a little bit more now as an adult, even decades later.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个曾经被拒绝的人，你现在作为一个成年人，可能会更容易看到拒绝，哪怕几十年后也是如此。

sentences.en: If you're someone that was never rejected, you were always popular.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个从未被拒绝、总是很受欢迎的人。

sentences.en: You might be bad at noticing signals that suggest danger or times when you might need some critical feedback.
sentences.zh: 你可能不善于注意到暗示危险的信号，或者那些你可能需要一些批判性反馈的时刻。

sentences.en: These kinds of ways in which we see the world are very, very much related to who we were back when we were in our teenage years.
sentences.zh: 我们看待世界的方式，与我们青少年的那段岁月有着非常、非常密切的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you wrote how popular teens and children are more likely to be happier, more successful and have better relationships as adults.
sentences.zh: 你写过受欢迎的青少年和儿童成年后更有可能更快乐、更成功并拥有更好的关系。

sentences.en: Well, that depends.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这得看情况。

sentences.en: So those who are popular can be two different groups.
sentences.zh: 所以受欢迎的人可以分为两类。

sentences.en: You have some who are popular when they were young and they would be the kind that we would call likable.
sentences.zh: 有些人在年轻时很受欢迎，他们属于我们称之为讨人喜欢的那种。

sentences.en: But then you have a different kind of popularity that emerges in adolescence.
sentences.zh: 但随后在青春期会出现另一种受欢迎。

sentences.en: We call that type of popularity status.
sentences.zh: 我们将这种类型的受欢迎称为地位。

sentences.en: And those are very different types of popularity.
sentences.zh: 这是两种截然不同的受欢迎类型。

sentences.en: Likeability is good.
sentences.zh: 讨人喜欢是好的。

sentences.en: Status is pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 地位则相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Can you describe what those two types of popularity mean a bit more?
sentences.zh: 你能多描述一下这两种受欢迎意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: What is status and what is likability?
sentences.zh: 什么是地位，什么是讨人喜欢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, likability is the kind of popularity that we have when we're really young.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，讨人喜欢是我们非常年轻时拥有的那种受欢迎。

sentences.en: And it used to be the kind of popularity that was important as you were an adult.
sentences.zh: 过去这也是你成年后很重要的一种受欢迎。

sentences.en: It's based on how much you make other people feel happy, valued and included.
sentences.zh: 它基于你让其他人感到快乐、有价值和被包容的程度。

sentences.en: And it doesn't mean that you're a pushover and you're making everyone feel better as opposed to fulfilling your own needs.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你是个唯唯诺诺的人，为了让每个人感觉更好而放弃满足自己的需求。

sentences.en: In fact, highly likable people are very likely to become leaders, but they do it in a way that's welcoming and inclusive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，极具讨人喜欢特质的人非常有可能成为领导者，但他们的方式是热情和包容的。

sentences.en: That's not what we all think of when we think about what popularity was like in high school.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我们所有人一想到高中时的受欢迎程度时所想的那样。

sentences.en: We think about what it was like to be cool.
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是那种很酷的感觉。

sentences.en: And that really translates scientifically to being known by everyone, being visible, being influential, dominant, and powerful.
sentences.zh: 在科学上，这实际上转化为被所有人认识、具有高可见度、有影响力、专横和强大。

sentences.en: That kind of popularity is called status.
sentences.zh: 这种受欢迎被称为地位。

sentences.en: And status has pretty bad long-term outcomes because what works for us in high school does not always work for us in the adult world.
sentences.zh: 而地位会带来相当糟糕的长期结果，因为我们在高中时行之有效的方法并不总是在成年人的世界里管用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And just because someone has status, you said dominance, doesn't necessarily mean people like them.
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅因为某人有地位，你提到了专横，并不一定意味着人们喜欢他们。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In fact, in high school, if you remember which kids were kind of the coolest that had the highest status, research says that at least half of the kids in school did not like
sentences.zh: 事实上，在高中里，如果你还记得哪些孩子比较酷且地位最高，研究表明至少有一半的孩子根本不喜欢

sentences.en: them at all.
sentences.zh: 他们。

sentences.en: In fact, they hated them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们讨厌他们。

sentences.en: But that didn't mean that they didn't regard them as being cool nevertheless.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们不认为对方依然很酷。

sentences.en: And the same thing happens in adulthood.
sentences.zh: 成年后也是如此。

sentences.en: We know that there are some people who have really high status.
sentences.zh: 我们知道有些人拥有极高的地位。

sentences.en: They are powerful and dominant and even aggressive.
sentences.zh: 他们强大、专横甚至具有攻击性。

sentences.en: And we can acknowledge that, but that doesn't mean we necessarily find them to be making us happy, feeling valued or included.
sentences.zh: 我们可以承认这一点，但这并不意味着我们一定觉得他们让我们感到快乐、有价值或被包容。

sentences.en: We don't like them.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: And it seems like when you're at that age, you are much more concerned about those people who do have that status.
sentences.zh: 似乎当你处于那个年龄时，你会更加关注那些确实拥有地位的人。

sentences.en: Whereas as adults, I think it's much easier to get away from people like that.
sentences.zh: 然而作为成年人，我认为要远离这样的人要容易得多。

sentences.en: Maybe not so much in the workplace, but in other aspects of your life, it just seems like it's easier to brush that off.
sentences.zh: 也许在职场中没那么容易，但在你生活的其他方面，似乎更容易把这当作浮云。

sentences.en: Is that a correct assessment that it's more difficult when you're younger to do that?
sentences.zh: 年轻时更难做到这一点，这种评估准确吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it makes perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: And some of the reason why is because we think that some of these changes in the brain really make us similar to a lot of other species.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为我们认为大脑中的某些变化确实让我们类似于许多其他物种。

sentences.en: A lot of mammalian species are interested in kind of that power and dominance and visibility because it gets you access to more resources, food or mating partners.
sentences.zh: 许多哺乳动物物种对这种权力和统治力以及可见度很感兴趣，因为这能让你获得更多的资源、食物或交配伙伴。

sentences.en: And our brains are acting like other mammals' brains.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑表现得像其他哺乳动物的大脑一样。

sentences.en: Even mice, when they reach their adolescent period, they're much less interested in hanging
sentences.zh: 即使是老鼠，当它们进入青春期时，它们对和成年老鼠闲逛的兴趣

sentences.en: out with adult mice as they are other adolescent mice because they're really interested in kind of that biologically programmed desire to have status.
sentences.zh: 远不如和其他青春期老鼠在一起，因为它们真的对这种生物学上编程决定的渴望地位的本能感兴趣。

sentences.en: So that's cool to do in high school.
sentences.zh: 所以在高中这样做是很酷的。

sentences.en: That's something that we're probably inevitably going to feel and we should expect our kids to feel that way when they reach adolescence.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可能会不可避免地感受到的东西，当我们的孩子进入青春期时，我们也应该预料到他们会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: But it used to be that we would stop caring about that kind of popularity when we graduated from high school.
sentences.zh: 但过去，当我们从高中毕业时，我们就不再在乎那种受欢迎程度了。

sentences.en: That's not the way the world works anymore, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，现在的世界可不是这样运作的了。

sentences.en: So you're saying people, we do care more about it maybe than some people realize.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是人们，我们确实比某些人意识到的更在乎它。

sentences.en: I think we do.
sentences.zh: 我想我们确实是的。

sentences.en: In fact, I think that we do now in this year than we ever did before in the history of our
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为今年我们对此的关心程度超过了我们物种历史上的任何时候

sentences.en: species because things have dramatically changed in the last 20 or 30 years in ways that now make us care about status more than we ever have before.
sentences.zh: 因为在过去20到30年里，事物发生了巨大的变化，以至于现在我们比以往任何时候都更加关心地位。

sentences.en: That's scary.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is the case?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么会这样？

sentences.en: There's a lot of interesting theories about why.
sentences.zh: 关于原因有很多有趣的理论。

sentences.en: You know, some people say that it started with CNN, believe it or not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人说这一切始于CNN，信不信由你。

sentences.en: That kind of 24-hour news cycle was the first time that we had to start changing the way that we talked about news and we made it a little bit more focused on people and people's
sentences.zh: 那种24小时滚动新闻周期是我们第一次不得不开始改变我们谈论新闻的方式，我们让它更多地聚焦于人物以及个人的

sentences.en: individual experiences.
sentences.zh: 经历。

sentences.en: And it suddenly changed.
sentences.zh: 它突然就变了。

sentences.en: Our view of celebrity and fame and status was not only afforded to a very few in an inaccessible way.
sentences.zh: 我们对名流、名气和地位的看法不再是少数人高不可攀的专利。

sentences.en: It suddenly became the case that almost anybody could have that moment, those 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，几乎任何人都可以拥有那个时刻，那15分钟的名气。

sentences.en: And some theories suggest that that was the beginning of a change in the way that we thought
sentences.zh: 有些理论表明，那是我们看待受欢迎方式发生转变的开始，这种转变如今反映在社交媒体或真人秀等事物中

sentences.en: about popularity, a change that today is reflected in things like social media or reality TV, you
sentences.zh: 你知道，这延伸了我们社会开始觉得我们所有人都能分一杯地位羹的想法。

sentences.en: know, extensions of the idea that our society started to feel that we could all get a piece of status.
sentences.zh: 过去可不是这样的。

sentences.en: It didn't used to be that way.
sentences.zh: 你认为这是否意味着今天的青少年生活比

sentences.en: Do you think that translates to life being more challenging for teens today than it was
sentences.zh: 20、30、40年前更具挑战性？

sentences.en: 20, 30, 40 years ago?
sentences.zh: 哦，我非常为今天的青少年感到担忧，因为他们生活在一个通过鼠标点击或在手机上24小时7天追求地位已经成为常态的世界里。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm so worried about teens today because they've lived in a world where pursuing status with a mouse click or on your phone 24-7, that's become normal.
sentences.zh: 当我为这本书工作时，我震惊地发现有那么多儿童和成人的

sentences.en: And when I worked on the book, I was shocked to find how many covers of magazines for both
sentences.zh: 杂志封面都在大力宣扬这样一种信息：我们应该关我们的点赞、

sentences.en: kids and for adults are really promoting the message that we should care about our likes and
sentences.zh: 转发和粉丝，甚至连孩子们都被鼓励在社交

sentences.en: our retweets and our followers and even kids are being encouraged to say things on social
sentences.zh: 媒体上说一些他们明知不相信的话，因为如果能给他们带来更多的赞或粉丝，那就值得了。

sentences.en: media that they explicitly don't believe because if it gets them more likes or followers, then it's worth it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想这给孩子们传递的信息，即地位比与其他人的真实联系或正直更重要，

sentences.en: And if you think about the message that that's sending the kids, that status is more important
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常可怕的信息。

sentences.en: than actual true connections with others or integrity, that's a really, really scary message.
sentences.zh: 你在书的开头提到，你希望它能成为人们重新审视我们文化的一种方式，正如你所提到的，它对名气、受欢迎程度、名声、权力、财富和名人的关注，以及它实际上是如何让我们变得不快乐的。

sentences.en: And you said at the top of your book that you want it to serve as a way for people to reconsider
sentences.zh: 你能详细阐述一下吗？

sentences.en: our culture, as you've mentioned, and its focus on fame, popularity, fame, power, wealth, and celebrity and how it's actually making us unhappy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，研究已经考察了地位的影响。

sentences.en: Can you elaborate on that a bit more?
sentences.zh: 一些研究观察了那些现在地位最高的人，也就是在我们的社会中拥有职位的人，

sentences.en: Well, research has looked at the effects of status.
sentences.zh: 可能是由于名气，或者是你在公司或政府中拥有其他类型的地位职位。

sentences.en: Some research has looked at those who are the highest status now, the people who hold positions
sentences.zh: 他们发现，那些处于最高地位职位的人患抑郁症的风险更高。

sentences.en: in our society, maybe due to celebrity or other kinds of positions of status in your company or in our government.
sentences.zh: 他们也更有可能从事各种行为，尤其是攻击性行为，仅仅是为了维持或永远试图提升他们的地位。

sentences.en: And what they find is that those people who are in the highest positions of status are at greater risk for depression.
sentences.zh: 这有点像一种成瘾。

sentences.en: They're also more likely to engage in behaviors, especially aggressive behaviors, just to maintain or forever attempt to increase their status.
sentences.zh: 一旦你拥有了地位或想要地位，你就永远不会满足。

sentences.en: It's kind of an addiction.
sentences.zh: 无论你在社会阶层中有多高，你总是在争夺更多地位的指标。

sentences.en: Once you have status or want status, you can never have enough.
sentences.zh: 还有一些研究调查了高中里那些酷炫的孩子后来怎么样了，也就是那些在地位方面最受欢迎的孩子。

sentences.en: No matter how high you are on the social hierarchy, you always are vying for more indicators of status.
sentences.zh: 像弗吉尼亚大学的乔·艾伦的研究，他对那些酷炫的孩子进行了几十年的追踪调查。

sentences.en: There's also been some research that's looked at what happened to those cool kids in high school, those kids that were the most popular in terms of status.
sentences.zh: 他发现，那些青少年时期非常酷的孩子长大后面临更高的成瘾、焦虑、抑郁风险，并且他们有关系问题。

sentences.en: Research like Joe Allen's research at University of Virginia, he's followed up those cool kids for decades.
sentences.zh: 他们在亲密关系中的满意度往往较低，并且更频繁地分手。

sentences.en: And what he's found is that those really cool kids as teenagers grow up to be at greater risk for addictions, anxiety, depression, and they have relationship probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着那些曾经受欢迎的儿童和青少年，可能是因为地位而不是讨人喜欢，但他们长大后更有可能变得不受欢迎且不太成功。

sentences.en: They tend to have lower satisfaction in relationships and they're more frequently broken up with.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that means that children and teens who were popular, maybe due to status, but not likability, but then they grew up to be most more likely to be unpopular and less successful.
sentences.zh: 研究非常清楚地表明，讨人喜欢孩子们，甚至早在幼儿园年龄就讨人喜欢的孩子，他们所获得的益处能持续几十年。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 他们赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: The research shows pretty clearly the likable kids, even the kids that are likable as early as kindergarten age, they have benefits that last for decades.
sentences.zh: 他们更快乐。

sentences.en: They make more money.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至更健康，寿命更长。

sentences.en: They're happier.
sentences.zh: 他们在婚姻、职场和家庭中的关系更好，甚至他们的孩子也过得更好。

sentences.en: They're even healthier and they live longer lives.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有更好的婚姻、职场和家庭关系，甚至他们的孩子也更优秀。

sentences.en: They have better marriages and relationships at work and at home and even their children do better.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有更好的婚姻和工作及家庭关系，甚至他们的孩子也更优秀。

sentences.en: So likability is extraordinarily powerful, which is interesting because we don't want to spend a lot of time teaching likability, but results say we should.
sentences.zh: 所以受欢迎程度是非常强大的，这很有趣，因为我们不想花大量时间来教导如何受欢迎，但研究结果表明我们应该这样做。

sentences.en: The opposite is the case for status.
sentences.zh: 地位则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Those who have high status grow up to have worse outcomes over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，那些拥有高地位的人长大后的结果往往更糟。

sentences.en: I think that's often reflected in some of the movies you see when you talk about what happens to the teens when they grow up.
sentences.zh: 我认为这经常反映在你看到的一些电影中，当你谈到青少年长大后会发生什么时。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of Can't Hardly Wait, if you remember that movie.
sentences.zh: 我想到了《窈窕美眉》，如果你还记得那部电影的话。

sentences.en: Oh, there's so many.
sentences.zh: 哦，有太多了。

sentences.en: That one's the one that comes to mind where they were doing like next year, this is what happened to the popular jock.
sentences.zh: 那部电影是我想到的其中之一，他们在里面展示了，比如第二年，那个受欢迎的运动员发生了什么。

sentences.en: He was like, uh, dropped out of college and worked at a car wash or something, you know, and gained 50 pounds, whatever the, whatever the case was.
sentences.zh: 他当时，呃，大学辍学了，在洗车场工作什么的，你知道，胖了50磅，不管，不管情况是怎样的。

sentences.en: And while the guy who was, um, the, the nerd type, if you will, he got the girl and he went off to college somewhere and had a great life.
sentences.zh: 而那个，嗯，书呆子类型的人，如果你愿意这么说的话，他赢得了女孩的芳心，去某个地方上大学，并过上了美好的生活。

sentences.en: Um, so, and we often hear stories about people who were rejected as teens who then flourish as adults.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我们经常听到一些故事，关于那些在青少年时期被拒绝，后来在成年后大放异彩的人。

sentences.en: So can a person's popularity change over time?
sentences.zh: 那么，一个人的受欢迎程度会随着时间改变吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然会。

sentences.en: So some of the ways in which we maintain our popularity is we are all caught in a vicious cycle that started when we were in high school.
sentences.zh: 所以我们维持受欢迎程度的一些方式是，我们都陷入了一个恶性循环，这个循环始于我们读高中的时候。

sentences.en: And most of us don't realize that we're in that cycle right now.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人并没有意识到我们现在正处于那个循环中。

sentences.en: And the way that it works is that we have these important formative experiences at the time when our brains are most sensitive to popularity.
sentences.zh: 它的运作方式是，在我们的大脑对受欢迎程度最敏感的时候，我们有这些重要的形成期经历。

sentences.en: We have experiences that stick with us for decades.
sentences.zh: 我们的经历会伴随我们几十年。

sentences.en: And whether we think about them overtly or not, they are influencing the way that we respond to every social interaction every single day.
sentences.zh: 无论我们是否有意去想它们，它们都在影响着我们每天对每一个社交互动的反应。

sentences.en: So people who felt rejected might not go to a party where they would have the opportunity to make new relationships, or they might go to that party and assume that people will
sentences.zh: 所以，那些感到被拒绝的人可能不会去参加一个本有机会建立新关系的派对，或者他们可能会去那个派对，并假设别人会

sentences.en: not like them.
sentences.zh: 不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: They might have their arms folded or not make eye contact or not, uh, create an overture when there could have been one.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会双臂抱胸，或者不进行眼神交流，或者在本来可以主动的时候，呃，不采取主动。

sentences.en: And without realizing it, they are perpetuating that, uh, self-fulfilling prophecy of creating
sentences.zh: 在没有意识到的情况下，他们正在延续那种，呃，自我实现的预言，即创造

sentences.en: a world, contributing to a world where they get rejected again and again to mirror what their expectations were, expectations that were built when they were adolescents.
sentences.zh: 一个世界，促成一个让他们一次又一次被拒绝的世界，以呼应他们的期望，这些期望是在他们青春期时建立的。

sentences.en: Um, what we can do to break that is recognize that we all have a bias, a bias that was built in the halls of high school, that's changing how we interact socially today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可以做些什么来打破这一点，那就是认识到我们都有一个偏见，这个偏见是在高中的大厅里建立的，它正在改变我们今天的社交互动方式。

sentences.en: We have to recognize what our personal bias is and try and challenge it and see if there might be ways to recognize that we are not 15 anymore and people are not going to relate
sentences.zh: 我们必须认识到我们的个人偏见是什么，并试着挑战它，看看是否有办法认识到我们已经不再是15岁了，人们不会像当年那样

sentences.en: to us the way they did back then.
sentences.zh: 对待我们。

sentences.en: It's absolutely fascinating that, you know, your life and who you were as a teen is affecting your life now.
sentences.zh: 绝对令人着迷的是，你知道，你的生活以及你十几岁时的你是如何影响你现在的生活的。

sentences.en: I mean, does that happen unconsciously?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是无意识发生的吗？

sentences.en: I'm assuming, right?
sentences.zh: 我想是的吧？

sentences.en: It's definitely on an implicit level, but there's been really interesting research to, you know, shed some light on that.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是在内隐层面上，但有一些非常有趣的研究，你知道，为这一点提供了一些光亮。

sentences.en: There was one study where they looked at people with and without kind of difficulties, uh, socially and they had them watch a movie.
sentences.zh: 曾有一项研究，他们观察了有社交困难和没有社交困难的人，并让他们看了一部电影。

sentences.en: They watched, they all watched the exact same movie, but they wore special eye tracking glasses
sentences.zh: 他们看了，他们都看了完全相同的电影，但他们戴了特殊的眼动追踪眼镜

sentences.en: so they could see what it is that people looked at and how long they looked at those parts of the movie.
sentences.zh: 这样研究人员就能看到人们看的是什么，以及他们看电影那些部分的时间有多长。

sentences.en: What they found was that people who had happy social lives in the past watch the movie and their eyes really focused on other happy social experiences.
sentences.zh: 他们发现的是，过去拥有快乐社交生活的人在看电影时，他们的目光真的集中在其他快乐的社交经历上。

sentences.en: People smiling and nodding and, um, gesturing for others to be included into social interactions.
sentences.zh: 人们微笑着、点着头，呃，做着手势邀请其他人融入社交互动中。

sentences.en: But when people with social difficulties watch the same exact movie, their eyes spent almost
sentences.zh: 但是当有社交困难的人看完全相同的电影时，他们的目光花了几乎

sentences.en: three quarters of the time staring at rejection cues, people that were frowning or looking away or turning their body posture away.
sentences.zh: 四分之三的时间盯着拒绝的信号，那些皱着眉头、把视线移开或者把身体姿势转开的人。

sentences.en: And it really, to me, just is shocking how much without realizing it, we are screening out
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这真的很令人震惊，在没有意识到的情况下，我们每天都在屏蔽掉

sentences.en: information in the world every day that confirms either our worst fears or our happiest memories.
sentences.zh: 世界上那些证实我们最坏的恐惧或最快乐的回忆的信息。

sentences.en: And again, a lot of that has to do with the experiences that we had when we first built these adult brains at the age of 12 to 15.
sentences.zh: 同样，这很大程度上与我们在12到15岁首次建立这些成年大脑时所经历的事情有关。

sentences.en: Do you have any tips about how to challenge those biases?
sentences.zh: 你有什么关于如何挑战这些偏见的建议吗？

sentences.en: One thing we can do is we can really start to try and get new data, trying to get new experiences that challenge our expectations.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做的一件事是，我们真的可以开始尝试获取新数据，尝试获得能够挑战我们期望的新体验。

sentences.en: And there are actually really simple ways to do that.
sentences.zh: 实际上有非常简单的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: There's a phenomenon called social mimicry that suggests that if we walk into a room with poor eye contact and with our arms folded, other people will pick up on that.
sentences.zh: 有一个被称为社会模仿的现象，它表明如果我们走进一个房间时缺乏眼神交流且双臂抱胸，其他人就会察觉到这一点。

sentences.en: They won't understand why, but they will start feeling sad and they will immediately make
sentences.zh: 他们不会明白为什么，但他们会开始感到悲伤，并且他们会立即对你做出

sentences.en: assumptions about you, suggesting that maybe you are not someone that they want to interact with.
sentences.zh: 假设，暗示你可能不是他们想要互动的人。

sentences.en: Sometimes we think of it the other way.
sentences.zh: 有时我们从相反的角度来看待它。

sentences.en: We notice someone that makes us feel happy and we have a good time.
sentences.zh: 我们注意到某个人让我们感到快乐，我们度过了一段美好的时光。

sentences.en: We kind of say something like, they have positive energy or, you know, you enjoy spending time with them.
sentences.zh: 我们有点像是在说，他们有积极的能量，或者，你知道，你喜欢和他们在一起。

sentences.en: It brings out your best self.
sentences.zh: 它能展现出你最好的一面。

sentences.en: That's social mimicry.
sentences.zh: 这就是社会模仿。

sentences.en: So a really good self-experiment is for someone to go in and try something different.
sentences.zh: 所以一个非常好的自我实验是让人走进去尝试一些不同的事情。

sentences.en: Try to walk in in a little bit of a good mood, maybe better than usual, or say hello to a few
sentences.zh: 试着带着一点好心情走进去，也许比平时更好，或者向比你平时

sentences.en: more people you normally would, or try and smile and keep your arms at your side rather than folded.
sentences.zh: 更多的人打招呼，或者试着微笑并把手臂放在身体两侧而不是双臂抱胸。

sentences.en: And people are surprised to see how quickly they can break the cycle just by eliciting from others a very different response to a social interaction.
sentences.zh: 人们惊讶地发现，仅仅通过引发其他人对社交互动的截然不同反应，他们能以多快的速度打破这个循环。

sentences.en: And once it happens one time, it starts to become, it starts to trigger more and more instances of where you can start changing those popularity dynamics in your life.
sentences.zh: 一旦发生了一次，它就开始变成，开始引发越来越多的情况，在这些情况下你可以开始改变你生活中的那些受欢迎程度的动态。

sentences.en: And going back to teenage years, in your book, you identified five distinct groups that we all fall into during that time in our lives.
sentences.zh: 回到青少年时期，在你的书中，你确定了在我们人生那个阶段我们都会落入的五个截然不同的群体。

sentences.en: And those were accepted, average, controversial, neglected, and rejected.
sentences.zh: 它们是：受欢迎型、普通型、争议型、被忽视型和被拒绝型。

sentences.en: Can you explain each one and what the benefits and concerns of each group are?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下每一个群体以及每个群体的好处和担忧是什么吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Those are five different types of likability.
sentences.zh: 那是五种不同类型的受欢迎程度。

sentences.en: And it's really based on the extent to which your peers select you as someone that they like the most or they like the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是基于你的同龄人选择你作为他们最喜欢的人或最不喜欢的人的程度。

sentences.en: It actually can be measured as young as the age of three years old, and it's remarkably stable over time.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可以在低至三岁的时候就被测量出来，而且随着时间的推移，它具有显着的稳定性。

sentences.en: The accepted kids tend to do really well.
sentences.zh: 受欢迎的孩子往往表现得非常好。

sentences.en: They're picked by others as being like the most, but rarely picked as like the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们被其他人选为最喜欢的，但很少被选为最不喜欢的。

sentences.en: And they tend to have lots of advantages and be more likely to become leaders.
sentences.zh: 他们往往拥有很多优势，并且更有可能成为领导者。

sentences.en: But the rejected kids have special powers also that's important.
sentences.zh: 但被拒绝的孩子也有特殊的能量，这也是很重要的。

sentences.en: They're often picked as being like the least and not picked as like the moSt.
sentences.zh: 他们经常被选为最不喜欢的，而不被选为最喜欢的。

sentences.en: But they tend to be particularly good at picking up on social cues suggesting rejection.
sentences.zh: 但他们往往特别擅长察觉暗示拒绝的社交信号。

sentences.en: And that can be very handy in a variety of different contexts.
sentences.zh: 这在各种不同的情境下都非常有用。

sentences.en: So don't rule out those who are rejected.
sentences.zh: 所以不要排除那些被拒绝的人。

sentences.en: Controversials tend to be picked as liked most and liked least and might be especially likely to have high status and be status seekers in adolescence.
sentences.zh: 争议型往往被选为最喜欢和最不喜欢的人，并且在青春期可能特别有可能拥有高地位并成为地位追求者。

sentences.en: Whereas the neglected kids are not picked as liked most or liked least by their peers.
sentences.zh: 而那些被忽视的孩子则不会被同龄人选为最喜欢或最不喜欢的人。

sentences.en: And research initially thought that these might be kids who have trouble, but that's not true.
sentences.zh: 研究最初认为这些可能是遇到困难的孩子，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: They tend to be highly adaptable from context to context and very likely to change to become accepted over time.
sentences.zh: 他们往往在不同的情境之间具有高度的适应性，并且随着时间的推移非常有可能转变为受欢迎的人。

sentences.en: So if you are in these groups, is that just a group you belong to because of who you are, your personality?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在这些群体中，这只是一个因为你是谁、你的个性而属于的群体吗？

sentences.en: Who, you know, is it just something that's inherent to all of us or are there ways to change this, to change which group we might belong to?
sentences.zh: 谁，你知道，这只是我们所有人固有的一些东西，还是有办法改变这一点，改变我们可能属于哪个群体？

sentences.en: We can absolutely change which group we belong to.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对可以改变我们属于哪个群体。

sentences.en: One of the biggest predictors of how likable we are and which of those groups we fall in is the extent to which we act aggressively or in pro-social ways.
sentences.zh: 我们有多受欢迎以及我们属于哪个群体的最大预测因素之一，是我们表现得具有攻击性还是具有亲社会行为的程度。

sentences.en: So aggressive kids are more likely to be controversial or rejected.
sentences.zh: 因此，具有攻击性的孩子更有可能是争议型或被拒绝型。

sentences.en: And we tend to learn a lot about aggressive behavior by watching our parents or others.
sentences.zh: 我们往往通过观察我们的父母或其他人来了解很多关于攻击性行为的知识。

sentences.en: But we can also engage in pro-social behaviors like paying attention to others, thinking about their needs, and engaging in behaviors that are welcoming and inclusive.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以参与亲社会行为，比如关注他人、思考他们的需求，以及参与欢迎和包容的行为。

sentences.en: Those are really powerful ways to make sure that we become accepted.
sentences.zh: 这些是确保我们变得受欢迎的非常强大的方法。

sentences.en: The same rules that apply when we were on the playground in elementary school also apply in the workplace today or in one day our retirement communities.
sentences.zh: 我们在小学操场上适用的规则同样适用于今天的职场，或者有一天在我们的退休社区里。

sentences.en: Those same dynamics play out in remarkably similar ways across the entire lifespan.
sentences.zh: 这些相同的动态在整个人生历程中以非常相似的方式上演。

sentences.en: And can you belong to more than one group at a time?
sentences.zh: 你能同时属于一个以上的群体吗？

sentences.en: Not typically, although there are some groups where it's easier to go between.
sentences.zh: 通常不会，尽管有些群体之间更容易转换。

sentences.en: So neglected kids are not likely to suddenly become controversial.
sentences.zh: 所以被忽视的孩子不太可能突然变成争议型。

sentences.en: But we might see neglected folks become rejected or accepted based on how they start acting in a new environment.
sentences.zh: 但根据他们在新的环境中的行为方式，我们可能会看到被忽视的人变得被拒绝或受欢迎。

sentences.en: And when teens and kids and teens get older, are there opportunities to change that?
sentences.zh: 当青少年和孩子以及青少年长大后，是否有机会改变这一点？

sentences.en: Like when they go to college, they're, you know, they're away from their home environment.
sentences.zh: 就像他们去上大学时，他们，你知道，他们离开了家庭环境。

sentences.en: They can kind of reinvent themselves, be a new person.
sentences.zh: 他们可以某种程度上重塑自己，成为一个新的人。

sentences.en: Is that an opportunity to maybe become a member of a different group that you weren't in when you were growing up?
sentences.zh: 这是一个机会，可以成为你在成长过程中不属于的另一个群体的成员吗？

sentences.en: It absolutely is possible.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是可能的。

sentences.en: It's not as easy as Freddie Prinze Jr.
sentences.zh: 它不像小弗雷迪·普林兹的

sentences.en: movies would make you believe, but it is possible to change.
sentences.zh: 电影让你相信的那样容易，但改变是可能的。

sentences.en: The problem is, is that we don't talk very much about popularity or likability.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们不太经常谈论受欢迎程度或喜爱度。

sentences.en: So we don't teach people what behaviors they should engage in to change.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没有教导人们应该进行哪些行为来改变。

sentences.en: There's research actually that shows that without any intervention, you can put a child into a brand new context.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有研究表明，在没有任何干预的情况下，你可以把一个孩子放到一个全新的环境中。

sentences.en: And within three hours, they have the same likable reputation that they had in their old context.
sentences.zh: 在三个小时内，他们就拥有了他们在旧环境中一样的受欢迎的名声。

sentences.en: So it's really important that we're talking about this and helping to teach kids why it's important to engage in likable behaviors.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论这个并帮助教导孩子们为什么参与受欢迎的行为很重要，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's certain approaches you want to take with that too, because you want to tell kids, you want to explain it, I'm sure in a healthy way saying like, you want to get
sentences.zh: 我确信你也有一些特定的方法想要用来处理这个问题，因为你想告诉孩子们，你想解释它，我确信是以一种健康的、说“你想与他人

sentences.en: along with others.
sentences.zh: 融洽相处”的方式。

sentences.en: You want to, you know, be a part of a group.
sentences.zh: 你想，你知道，成为群体的一部分。

sentences.en: You want to be, you know, liked in some ways without making them feel like they are sacrificing who they are to please others.
sentences.zh: 你想，你知道，在某些方面被人喜欢，而不会让他们觉得为了取悦他人而牺牲了真正的自我。

sentences.en: How would you go about telling a child or a teen to, how to do that?
sentences.zh: 你会如何着手告诉一个孩子或青少年如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全对。

sentences.en: It's really important that kids know, just like adults, that we are going to be valued for being who we are.
sentences.zh: 让孩子们像成年人一样知道我们因做自己而受到重视，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: We just have to make sure that the way that we are is not somehow making other people feel inferior or dominated or somehow like they're not welcome as a member of the community.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要确保我们的这种方式不会以某种方式让其他人感到自卑、被支配，或者觉得他们作为社区的一员不受欢迎。

sentences.en: That's a really important message that unfortunately we've forgotten.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的信息，不幸的是我们已经忘记了。

sentences.en: Perhaps now in this day, more than years past, where we live in a society that's really about promoting our own voice rather than thinking of ways to help others feel connected and
sentences.zh: 也许现在在这个时代，比过去几年更是如此，我们生活在一个真正关乎宣扬我们自己的声音而非思考如何帮助他人感到联系和

sentences.en: genuinely cared for as a community.
sentences.zh: 作为社区被真诚关怀的社会中。

sentences.en: And what advice do you have for parents of kids who are not popular?
sentences.zh: 对于那些不受欢迎的孩子的父母，你有什么建议？

sentences.en: So they might fall into that neglected or rejected group.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会落入那个被忽视或被拒绝的群体。

sentences.en: What can they do?
sentences.zh: 他们能做什么？

sentences.en: I think it's really important for parents to think about how they can help their kids' social behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我认为父母思考如何帮助孩子的社交行为非常重要。

sentences.en: But parents have to be realistic and honest about the ways in which their child might interact.
sentences.zh: 但父母必须对孩子互动的方式保持现实和诚实。

sentences.en: First of all, I would say that I wouldn't want any parent to freak out if their kids were rejected because there's a lot of research to suggest that having one or two very good
sentences.zh: 首先，我要说的是，我不希望任何父母在他们的孩子被拒绝时惊慌失措，因为有很多研究表明，拥有一两个非常好的

sentences.en: friends can be really, really important and compensatory for folks who are having a tough time with rejection.
sentences.zh: 朋友可以非常非常重要，并且能够对那些在拒绝中经历艰难时期的人起到补偿作用。

sentences.en: So that might be the first goal, is to really think about how to foster a couple of friendships.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是第一个目标，即真正思考如何培养几段友谊。

sentences.en: But if a child is experiencing difficulties with rejection, it's important to really look
sentences.zh: 但如果一个孩子正在经历拒绝带来的困难，真正审视

sentences.en: at whether that child might be acting aggressively or doing other things that make them not respectful of the social norMs.
sentences.zh: 这个孩子是否表现出攻击性或做其他不尊重社会规范的事情，这很重要。

sentences.en: An example might be a kid who very pleasantly suggests an activity to play in, kind of let's all play Legos while everyone else is playing with cars.
sentences.zh: 一个例子可能是一个孩子非常愉快地建议一个游玩活动，比如当其他所有人都在玩汽车时，让我们大家都来玩乐高吧。

sentences.en: But instead of doing it in a way that seems to be respectful of what everyone else is already
sentences.zh: 但他们做这件事的方式似乎并不尊重其他所有人

sentences.en: playing, they might do it in a very abrupt way that comes across as awkward and disruptive.
sentences.zh: 已经在玩的游戏，而是以一种非常唐突的方式进行，显得有些尴尬和具有破坏性。

sentences.en: That sometimes is the difficulty.
sentences.zh: 这有时就是困难所在。

sentences.en: And it is something that can be trained.
sentences.zh: 而且这是可以经过训练来改变的。

sentences.en: And if you were that kid who was bullied or you were in that rejected group growing up during these crucial years, how can you find maybe some healing as adults?
sentences.zh: 如果你曾是那个被霸凌的孩子，或者在这些关键成长年头里属于那个被拒绝的群体，作为成年人，你该如何找到某种疗愈呢？

sentences.en: Because we often hear about the long lasting impacts of being bullied or rejected because of whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 因为我们经常听到被霸凌或因各种原因被拒绝所带来的长期影响。

sentences.en: So how can you yourself get over that experience and help to thrive as an adult?
sentences.zh: 所以你自己如何才能走出那段经历并在成年后茁壮成长？

sentences.en: I wish that everybody knew about research on bullies that shows that in many cases, it's bullying that is related to serious emotional difficulties.
sentences.zh: 我希望每个人都知道关于霸凌者的研究，该研究表明，在许多情况下，正是霸凌与严重的悲伤情绪困难有关。

sentences.en: And it might be helpful for those who were victims to recognize that they were victimized
sentences.zh: 对于受害者来说，认识到他们成为受害者

sentences.en: not often because of their own weaknesses or any kind of difficulties that they may have experienced.
sentences.zh: 往往不是因为他们自己的弱点或他们可能经历过的任何种类的困难，这可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: But it really is more of a sign of how much bullies themselves were suffering from emotional distress
sentences.zh: 但这实际上更多地说明了霸凌者自身在多大程度上遭受着情绪困扰，

sentences.en: where they were exposed to that kind of aggressive behavior somewhere in their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们在生活中的某个地方接触过那种攻击性行为。

sentences.en: The more we can move away from making personal attributions, from blaming ourselves, from being
sentences.zh: 我们越是能从归咎个人属性、从责备自己、从扮演

sentences.en: a victim, I think the easier it would be to cope with and recognize that it was the bully that probably was experiencing a lot of difficulties.
sentences.zh: 受害者的心态中走出来，我认为就越容易应对并认识到，很可能是那个霸凌者在经历许多困难。

sentences.en: And the victim might have been the unfortunate recipient of that.
sentences.zh: 而受害者可能只是不幸的承受者。

sentences.en: But it doesn't mean that someone actually had any personal weaknesses that were worth being victimized about.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着某人真的有什么值得被霸凌的个人弱点。

sentences.en: And on the flip side of all this, so for parents of kids who are really popular, either because
sentences.zh: 而所有这一切的另一面是，对于那些因为地位或受欢迎程度而真正受欢迎的孩子的父母来说，

sentences.en: of status or likability, and this might be a two-part question because those are very different aspects of being popular, what do those parents need to know?
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个两部分的问题，因为那是受欢迎的非常不同的两个方面，这些父母需要知道什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think that for parents of likable kids, that's terrific.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为对于受欢迎的孩子的父母来说，那太棒了。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a really good opportunity to really positively reinforce how kids are making others feel welcome and how they're being sensitive to other kids' feelings.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的机会，可以积极强化孩子们是如何让其他人感到受欢迎的，以及他们是如何对其他孩子的感受保持敏感的。

sentences.en: So that might be something that parents want to really look out for and find opportunities
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是父母想要真正关注并寻找机会去

sentences.en: to reinforce and help them generalize as they enter a world that values those behaviors, sadly, less and less.
sentences.zh: 强化和帮助他们推广的事情，当他们进入一个越来越少地重视这些行为的世界时。

sentences.en: But for kids who are high in status, it's going to be very, very hard to get kids to not be interested in status.
sentences.zh: 但对于地位高的孩子来说，要让孩子们对地位不感兴趣将是非常非常困难的。

sentences.en: I would recommend that parents remind those high-status kids that it's important to be likable too.
sentences.zh: 我建议父母提醒那些高地位的孩子，受欢迎也很重要。

sentences.en: You can be cool and dominant and highly influential and visible, and you're not going to convince anyone not to be.
sentences.zh: 你可以很酷、很有统治力、极具影响力和显眼，你无法说服任何人不去这样。

sentences.en: But remind them that they should not maintain that by putting others down, by being aggressive and being so overly focused on status that they're constantly seeking for more.
sentences.zh: 但要提醒他们，他们不应该通过贬低他人、表现出攻击性以及过度关注地位以至于不断寻求更多来维持这种状态。

sentences.en: Instead, teach them that while they might enjoy high status, they should also take time to let others feel included.
sentences.zh: 相反，教导他们虽然他们可能享受高地位，但他们也应该花时间让其他人感到被包容。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it's not going to reduce their status, but it is going to help them develop the skills they'll need for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这不会降低他们的地位，但确实会帮助他们培养未来几十年所需的技能。

sentences.en: Can young people choose the type of popularity they want, especially today in this ranking culture with social media being involved in every aspect of our teens' lives?
sentences.zh: 年轻人能选择他们想要的受欢迎程度吗？特别是在当今这个社交媒体渗透到青少年生活方方面面的排行榜文化中？

sentences.en: And it seems like we can't go back from that.
sentences.zh: 而且我们似乎已经回不了头了。

sentences.en: There's no putting the genie back in the bottle, if you will, and changing what teens are facing today in terms of the internet and social media.
sentences.zh: 可以说，木已成舟，无法回到过去，也没法改变青少年当下面临的互联网和社交媒体环境。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think social media is here to stay.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为社交媒体会一直存在下去。

sentences.en: The platforms change often, but I think the teens have grown up not knowing anything but.
sentences.zh: 平台经常更换，但我认为青少年成长过程中接触的就只有这些。

sentences.en: And it's important that we acknowledge that there's something very reinforcing, even biologically addictive, about social media that's going to be hard to change.
sentences.zh: 我们必须认识到，社交媒体有一种很强的强化作用，甚至是生物学上的成瘾性，这是很难改变的。

sentences.en: So I suggest moderation.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议适度使用。

sentences.en: I think it's important that we allow teens to participate on social media.
sentences.zh: 我认为允许青少年参与社交媒体是很重要的。

sentences.en: There's actually a lot of benefits that come from social media as well to adolescents, but we help them to also sometimes get off social media or use social media to promote actual
sentences.zh: 实际上，社交媒体对青少年也有很多好处，但我们要帮助他们有时也离开社交媒体，或者利用社交媒体来促进真正的

sentences.en: face-to-face or voice-to-voice interactions as well, because there's still a place for that, and that's still important for child development.
sentences.zh: 面对面或语音交流，因为这仍然有一席之地，对儿童发展也很重要。

sentences.en: We can help teens think about how to use the direct message functions or how to use the information they learn online to bring up in conversations offline.
sentences.zh: 我们可以帮助青少年思考如何使用私信功能，或者如何将在网上学到的信息带到线下的对话中。

sentences.en: We also need to have parents talking a little bit more, according to research, about how kids are consuming the information they see on social media.
sentences.zh: 根据研究，我们还需要让父母更多地讨论孩子们是如何消费他们在社交媒体上看到的信息的。

sentences.en: Do they recognize that kids are liking one another's posts because they're fronting or because
sentences.zh: 他们是否意识到，孩子们点赞彼此的帖子是因为他们在装腔作势，还是因为

sentences.en: they are doing it to save face or maintain friendships, not because they necessarily agree with every value and behavior that's expressed in social media posts.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是为了保住面子或维持友谊，而不是因为他们必然同意社交媒体帖子中表达的每一种价值观和行为。

sentences.en: I think digital media literacy is an untapped need within our school systems and among parent-child discussions that's really, really important in today's day and age.
sentences.zh: 我认为数字媒体素养是我们学校系统和亲子讨论中一个尚未充分挖掘的需求，在当今时代真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: Can adults choose the type of popularity they want?
sentences.zh: 成年人能选择他们想要的受欢迎程度吗？

sentences.en: You know, meaning, I mean, is status inherent or likability?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，地位是天生的还是喜爱度？

sentences.en: It seems like there's some push-pull on that that you can work on.
sentences.zh: 这其中似乎有一些你可以努力的拉锯。

sentences.en: You mentioned a bit throughout the podcast, you can work on your likability skills.
sentences.zh: 你在播客中多次提到，你可以培养你的讨喜能力。

sentences.en: So adults, can they choose how to be the type of popularity they want?
sentences.zh: 那么成年人，他们能选择如何成为他们想要的受欢迎类型吗？

sentences.en: I think we are making those choices hundreds of times a day without realizing that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们每天都在不知不觉中做出数百次这样的选择。

sentences.en: When we speak up in a meeting, when we decide what we're going to wear, when we decide what we're going to buy, when we decide what kind of interactions we want to engage in or how
sentences.zh: 当我们会议上发言时，当我们决定穿什么时，当我们决定买什么时，当我们决定参与什么样的互动时，或者

sentences.en: much time we want to spend on our own social media feeds, we are making the choice.
sentences.zh: 当我们决定花多少时间在自己的社交媒体动态上时，我们其实都在做出选择。

sentences.en: Are we trying to make ourselves stand out and seem somehow better than the rest of the crowd?
sentences.zh: 我们是想让自己脱颖而出，显得比其他人更好吗？

sentences.en: Are we trying to garner more power and influence?
sentences.zh: 我们是在试图获取更多的权力和影响力吗？

sentences.en: Or are we making choices that signal to others that we care about them feeling valued, that we
sentences.zh: 还是我们在做出这样的选择：向他人传递我们关心他们的价值，我们

sentences.en: want others to feel included, and that we are more interested in creating connection and community than we are in making ourselves seem like we are better than others?
sentences.zh: 希望他人感到被包容，并且我们对建立联系和社群的兴趣，远大于让自己显得比别人优秀的兴趣？

sentences.en: I think we make hundreds of those choices a day.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们每天都要做出数百次这样的选择。

sentences.en: And I hope that once people know about the two different types of popularity, it will give them some insight into how to make those choices wisely each day.
sentences.zh: 我希望一旦人们了解了这两种不同类型的受欢迎程度，就能让他们对每天如何明智地做出这些选择有一些启发。

sentences.en: And last question, I hope this is a fun one.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，希望这是一个轻松有趣的问题。

sentences.en: What teen movie do you think best depicts everything we've discussed today?
sentences.zh: 你认为哪部青春电影最能刻画我们今天讨论的所有内容？

sentences.en: Oh, there's so many that I think are important.
sentences.zh: 噢，有太多部我认为很重要的了。

sentences.en: I think Never Been Kissed is a great one.
sentences.zh: 我觉得《一吻定江山》就是一部很好的电影。

sentences.en: I think Breakfast Club is a great example of popularity in high school and the different groups that are out there.
sentences.zh: 我认为《早餐俱乐部》很好地展现了高中的受欢迎程度以及存在的不同群体。

sentences.en: There's just so many, honestly, that I think are important.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这样的电影实在太多了，我认为都很重要。

sentences.en: And it's interesting to me that a topic that we don't spend a whole lot of time investing policy dollars in or educational time in is the one way that we all, Hollywood and each
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们没有花太多政策资金或教育时间去投入的一个话题，却正是我们所有人——好莱坞以及我们每一个人——铭记青春期的方式。

sentences.en: of us, remembers our adolescence.
sentences.zh: 我们思考青少年时期，就离不开受欢迎程度。

sentences.en: We can't think about our teenage years without thinking about popularity.
sentences.zh: 这可能也就是为什么我们觉得那些青春电影如此重要，因为它们是一种方式，帮我们梳理大家作为青少年时都普遍经历过的事情。

sentences.en: And it's probably why we find those teen movies to be so important as a way of kind of working through what we all ubiquitously, universally went through when we were teenagers.
